results.reason: The response never identifies the Varga stock purchase as a Change of Control that needs Crestline consent under §15.4. It never says that Disclosure Schedule 3.5 wrongly treats the Crestline agreement as notice-only. It only notes that Crestline lacks change-of-control protection in the other direction, and it treats item 3.4's description as incomplete in a different respect.

Issue 2 explains that §14.2 together with the §1.1 'Qualified Transferee' definition lets Crestline assign without consent to any Territory distributor of laboratory or diagnostic products. It also notes the definition has no exclusion for competitors or their affiliates.

Issue 1 explains that First Amendment §3.1 restates §12.3 so only §9 breaches are carved out. It says the §10 and §11 carve-outs are dropped, cites §17.5 precedence, and concludes Crestline's IP breaches and indemnity are now capped.
The response states that the original §12.3 excluded 'breaches of Sections 9 and 10, and indemnification obligations under Section 11.'
The response states that the §12.2 cap is the amounts paid or payable to the Supplier in the 12 months preceding the claim.
The response is a memo with separately numbered issues. Each issue has headings for document/section, why it matters for Halvorsen, and a recommended fix.
The response does not conclude that the acquisition requires only notice to Crestline or that no consent is needed. It does not address that question at all.
The response concludes that the carve-outs were removed and that the amendment controls. It does not say they still apply.
